metadata.title: Phonon excitation and instabilities in biased graphene nanoconstrictions
metadata.authors: Tue Gunst, Jing-Tao Lu, Per Hedegard, Mads Brandbyge
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced. arXiv:1305.5907.

nodes.name: Graphene Nanoconstriction (GNC)
nodes.statement: A short graphene ribbon at the narrowest point of a constriction through which the current is passed; in this work, a small hydrogen-passivated GNC is studied (Fig. 1).

nodes.name: Mass-scaled ion displacements $Q$
nodes.statement: Vector $Q$ of mass-scaled ionic displacements used as the dynamical variable in the semi-classical generalized Langevin equation governing GNC vibrations.

nodes.name: Hilbert transform $H$
nodes.statement: $H\{g(x')\}(x) = \frac{1}{\pi} \mathrm{P} \int \frac{g(x')}{x' - x} \, dx'$, the principal-value Hilbert transform.

nodes.name: Inverse quality factor $1/Q$
nodes.statement: $1/Q = -2 \mathrm{Im}(\omega)/\mathrm{Re}(\omega) = 1/Q_{ph} + 1/Q_{el}(V_a)$, the per-period energy loss split into phonon-bath and electronic contributions.

nodes.name: Runaway mode
nodes.statement: A phonon mode with negative damping ($1/Q < 0$) that becomes unstable above a bias threshold; appears as a negative DOS peak around $\omega_0 \approx 170$ meV.

nodes.name: IETS mode
nodes.statement: Phonon mode with the largest inelastic tunnel spectroscopy signal in the electronic current and largest noise $S_{f,ii}(\omega_i)$; remains stable ($1/Q > 0$) under bias.

nodes.name: Semi-classical generalized Langevin equation (SCLE)
nodes.statement: $\ddot{Q}(t) = -K Q(t) - \int_{-\infty}^{t} \Pi^{r}(t-t') Q(t') \, dt' + f(t)$, with force-constant matrix $K$, retarded phonon self-energy $\Pi^r = \Pi^r_e + \Pi^r_{ph}$, and noise force $f(t)$.

nodes.name: Retarded electronic phonon self-energy
nodes.statement: $\Pi^{re}(\omega) = i\pi \mathrm{Re}\Lambda(\omega) - \pi \mathrm{Im}\Lambda(\omega) + \pi H\{\mathrm{Re}\Lambda(\omega')\}(\omega) + i\pi H\{\mathrm{Im}\Lambda(\omega')\}(\omega)$; the four terms yield electronic friction, non-conservative wind, renormalization, and Berry forces.

nodes.name: Interaction-weighted electron-hole pair density of states $\Lambda_{\alpha\beta}$
nodes.statement: $\Lambda_{\alpha\beta}(\omega) \equiv 2 \int \frac{d\epsilon}{4\pi^2} \mathrm{Tr}[M_k A_\alpha(\epsilon+\omega) M_l A_\beta(\epsilon)] \times [n_F(\epsilon+\omega-\mu_\alpha) - n_F(\epsilon-\mu_\beta)]$, with $\Lambda = \sum_{\alpha\beta} \Lambda_{\alpha\beta}$.

nodes.name: Noise spectral density $S_f$
nodes.statement: $S_f(\omega) = -\pi \Lambda(\omega) \coth(\frac{\omega}{2 k_B T}) - \pi \sum_{\alpha\beta} \Lambda_{\alpha\beta}(\omega) [\coth(\frac{\omega - (\mu_\alpha - \mu_\beta)}{2 k_B T}) - \coth(\frac{\omega}{2 k_B T})]$, including Joule heating contributions.

nodes.name: Nonequilibrium retarded phonon Green's function
nodes.statement: $D^r(\omega) = (D^a(\omega))^\dagger = [(\omega + i\eta)^2 - K - \Pi^r(\omega)]^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Average phonon kinetic energy
nodes.statement: $E_{\mathrm{kin}} = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \frac{d\omega}{2\pi} \omega^2 \mathrm{Tr}[D^r(\omega) S_f(\omega) D^a(\omega)]$, the phonon excitation in terms of the average kinetic energy.

nodes.name: Master equation for phonon number
nodes.statement: $\dot{N} = B(N+1) - A N$, with $A$ the absorption rate and $B$ the emission rate of phonons.

nodes.name: Fermi golden rule rates $A$, $B$
nodes.statement: $B \approx \int_{\mu_R + \hbar\omega_0}^{\mu_L} |\langle \psi_L(\epsilon) | M | \psi_R(\epsilon - \hbar\omega_0) \rangle|^2 \frac{d\epsilon}{2\pi}$ and $A \approx \int_{\mu_R - \hbar\omega_0}^{\mu_L} |\langle \psi_L(\epsilon) | M | \psi_R(\epsilon + \hbar\omega_0) \rangle|^2 \frac{d\epsilon}{2\pi}$, valid for $k_B T \ll \hbar\omega_0 < e V_a$.

nodes.name: Electronic friction in terms of $A-B$
nodes.statement: $A - B = -2\pi \sum_{\alpha\beta} \Lambda_{\alpha\beta}(\omega)$; the difference of absorption and emission rates equals the electronic friction.

nodes.name: DFT-NEGF computation of SCLE parameters
nodes.statement: Compute all SCLE parameters in the presence of current using first-principles DFT and nonequilibrium Green's functions, with electron-phonon interaction restricted to the high-current GNC region.

nodes.name: Limit electronic basis
nodes.statement: Expand the retarded Green's function and $A_\alpha$ in the eigenspace of $H + \Sigma_0(E_F)$ (slowly varying with energy) and limit to 200 states in $[-7, 6]$ eV around $E_F$.

nodes.name: Parallel computation of $\Lambda$
nodes.statement: Compute $\Lambda(\omega)$ in Eq. (3) by parallel execution over the $\omega$ and $V_a$ parameters, going beyond the wide-band approximation.

nodes.name: Assemble self-energies and Green's function
nodes.statement: Form $\Pi^r$ via Eq. (2) and obtain $D^r(\omega)$ via Eq. (5); compute heating $E_{\mathrm{kin}}$ via Eq. (6).

nodes.name: Current-induced phonon excitation in biased GNCs
nodes.statement: Determine the phonon excitation, current-induced forces, and stability of a biased graphene nanoconstriction at high current density, including Joule heating, electronic friction, wind, and Berry-phase forces.

nodes.name: Negative DOS at runaway frequency
nodes.statement: At $V_a \approx 0.5$ V the phonon DOS becomes negative at $\omega \approx 170$ meV, signaling a negatively damped (runaway) mode.
assumptions: GNC gated to second resonance peak

nodes.name: Heating divergence at runaway threshold
nodes.statement: From Eq. (6), the runaway gives a divergence of the current-induced change in $E_{\mathrm{kin}}$ at $V_a \approx 0.4$ V, signifying an instability in the harmonic approximation.

nodes.name: Bias-dependent electronic friction drives instability
nodes.statement: The instability is traced to the bias-dependent electronic friction; it disappears when the friction is held at its zero-bias value.
conclusions: Instability vanishes when electronic friction is fixed at zero-bias value
Bias dependence of friction is the necessary ingredient

nodes.name: Role of electrode-phonon damping
nodes.statement: Heating increases by an order of magnitude when the electrode-phonon bath is neglected; without phonon-bath damping, runaway begins already at $V_a \approx 0.15$ V with $>15$ runaway modes by $V_a \approx 0.4$ V.
assumptions: Compare full calculation vs. neglecting phonon-bath damping
conclusions: Phonon-bath damping is crucial in suppressing runaway
Without it, multiple runaway modes appear at low bias

nodes.name: Symmetry origin of negative friction
nodes.statement: For the runaway mode, $\psi_R(E_F + \omega_0)$ has nearly the same symmetry as $\psi_L^*(E_F)$ while $\psi_R(E_F - \omega_0)$ differs significantly, yielding very low absorption and high emission matrix elements; large phonon energies and the linear graphene DOS strengthen this symmetry breaking.
conclusions: $B > A$ for the runaway mode at sufficient bias
Negative electronic friction in graphene nanostructures is generic

nodes.name: Hydrogen-passivated GNC at $V_a = 0.5$ V
nodes.statement: DFT-NEGF computation of a hydrogen-passivated graphene nanoconstriction gated to its second transmission peak, exhibiting two resonance peaks (edge-localized 1st, center-localized 2nd) and a runaway mode at $\omega_0 \approx 170$ meV for $V_a \gtrsim 0.4$ V.

nodes.name: Runaway and IETS modes at $V_a = 0.4$ V
nodes.statement: Two degenerate modes at $V_a = 0.4$ V with $\omega_0 \approx 170$ meV: the runaway mode breaks left-right symmetry and becomes unstable, while the IETS mode yields the largest inelastic signal and remains stable.

nodes.name: Wind and Berry-phase forces lower runaway threshold
nodes.statement: Wind and Berry-phase forces are of the same order for the runaway mode; while not themselves causing the first runaway, they lower its bias threshold.

nodes.name: Generic graphene phenomenon
nodes.statement: Negative friction is generic in graphene nanostructures because high phonon energies produce markedly different symmetry of electronic states involved in emission vs. absorption, giving asymmetric matrix elements; gating in 2D systems makes graphene a test bed for such effects.
